question: A 32-year-old presents with a fracture of the distal third of the radius. The emergency physician asks whether this can be managed in a cast. The correct management decision is:

answers.text: Above-elbow cast for 6 weeks — acceptable non-operative treatment for an isolated distal radius fracture

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: An isolated distal radius fracture could be managed non-operatively, but a distal radial fracture must be assessed for DRUJ disruption. If there is DRUJ involvement, this is a Galeazzi injury and cast treatment has unacceptably high failure rates.

answers.text: Check for DRUJ instability; if present (Galeazzi fracture-dislocation), operative fixation with ORIF of the radius and DRUJ reduction is required — non-operative treatment is unreliable

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The Galeazzi fracture-dislocation is called a 'fracture of necessity' because cast immobilisation consistently fails to maintain DRUJ reduction. ORIF of the radial shaft restores length, and DRUJ stability is then assessed; if unstable, above-elbow cast in supination (or temporary K-wire) is added.

answers.text: Check for PRUJ dislocation — if the radial head is dislocated, this is a Galeazzi injury requiring surgery

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A distal radial fracture with radial head dislocation would be unusual; radial head dislocation with proximal ulna fracture is a Monteggia injury. Galeazzi involves DRUJ (distal radioulnar joint), not PRUJ.

answers.text: Closed reduction under anaesthesia; if the DRUJ reduces, immobilise in a below-elbow cast

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Closed reduction alone is not reliable for Galeazzi injuries. The DRUJ re-dislocates because the soft-tissue constraints are disrupted. ORIF of the radius is mandatory.

overallFeedback.feedback: The distal radius fracture must be assessed for DRUJ disruption. A Galeazzi fracture-dislocation cannot be reliably managed non-operatively — ORIF is required.
Correct. Galeazzi fracture-dislocation is the 'fracture of necessity' — ORIF is mandatory because conservative treatment invariably fails to hold DRUJ reduction.
